title: The Durable Frame · Phase 01

provenance.source_note: The approved six-week Forge program. This reading page does not set athlete position or file completed sessions.

weekly_structure.timing: After your main running workout when practical.
Full session only when you have recovered from Tuesday and Thursday running is easy.
After you have recovered from Saturday’s long run.

global_rules: Use your current working weights. Record the weight, reps and how many more good reps you could do. Do not test your maximum.
When every set reaches the top of its rep range with good form and about two good reps left, add the smallest available weight next time.
If your equipment cannot go heavier, use only a change in reps, tempo or exercise variation that Brice has given you.
Keep to the three sessions. Do not add a fourth day, bonus sets or extra exercises.

Do the full Thursday session only when you have recovered from Tuesday and Thursday running is easy. If Thursday has intervals, a tempo run or hill repeats, do only the calf raise, suitcase march and side plank, or skip strength.
Do not move missed Thursday work to Friday or Saturday.
If strength keeps making your main runs harder for more than a week, reduce the strength work with Brice before changing the running.

weeks.label: Start here

exercises.cue: Use your current working load. Clean reps, no max testing. Progress only after the top of the range is repeatable with reserve.
Brace the trunk. Pull without rotating. Record the actual kettlebell load used.
Stay tall through the trunk. No backbend.
Use the lightest available implement that keeps the shoulder doing the work.
Elbows wide. Keep the load honest and the upper back quiet.
No hip drive. Add load only after clean top-range reps.
Stop with about two reps available. This is not a burnout.
Full lower-body session only when Tuesday was controlled and recovery is normal. Rear-foot elevation is optional and requires a stable surface.
Controlled eccentric. If FORM Thursday carries real quality, skip this lower-body slot rather than creating workout debt.
Add kettlebell load only when the full range stays clean.
30–45 seconds per side. Hold the kettlebell without leaning. When Thursday running is quality, this trunk slot may remain while lower-body lifts are removed.
30–45 seconds per side. Straight line from shoulder to ankle.
Own the torso angle. Use the current working load as calibration, not as a test.
Use the version that loads the chest cleanly with the equipment available.
Keep ribs controlled. Reach long without turning it into a triceps exercise.
Finish each side with reserve. Do not chase a grind after Saturday's long run.
Rear shoulder and upper back. Keep the elbows wide.
Pause at the top. No rolling.
No hip drive. Keep about two reps available.
Stop about two reps before failure. Not a burnout.
